obligations.reason: The construction explicitly assumes the same full A=K+wH family, fixed K/pi/destruction, whole w box, all-start block q/tau, zero-mass residual and nonexpansive remainder. Nominal K rho is not transferred to A. E=abs(eta), coarse l1=4E and fixed signed scalar d_c are preserved.

Endpoint minima suffice for linear/concave quadratics. A convex quadratic additionally needs its strict-interior vertex value. The exact rational endpoint/vertex criterion is necessary and sufficient for interval nonnegativity and permits negative inner Bernstein coefficients. It is distinct from the physical whole-domain forcing-bound premise.

Splitting at the union of both source quadratics' strict-interior vertices makes each restriction monotone and nonnegative. For a quadratic, the middle coefficient is P(0)+D P'(0)/2=P(D)-D P'(D)/2 and is nonnegative using the appropriate monotonicity sign. At most two extra knots per original cell gives Neffective<=3Noriginal. Coincident vertices are deduplicated.

The primitive of (s-1/4)^2 has cubic Bernstein coefficients (0,1/48,-1/24,7/48). Thus the quadratic monotonicity argument cannot be applied automatically to a cubic. This exact counterexample only rejects that intermediate inference; it does not assert a broad no-go theorem.

The union of effective source knots shifted by k*tau and observation knots fixes every max/min overlap branch and empty/nonempty transition in each base-cell interior. Initial kernel jumps are present because t0 is an effective knot. A shift by Bmax+1 is outside the horizon. No derivative root is used as a propagation clock.

Simpson's identity is exact for the already supplied quadratic g_r. Each g_r(L), g_r(M), g_r(U) is a source restriction with nonnegative quadratic coefficients. Multiplying its weighted sum by the nonnegative affine overlap width yields exactly the four displayed B1*B2/6 cubic coefficients, including the denominators 6/18/18/6. This is not sampling an unknown forcing.

All original source cells remain in the convolution sum from original t0. q=0 keeps h0=1 and fresh age-strip-zero forcing; q=1 has no singular denominator. Source/observation refinement does not reset the memory. The J0/J1/J2 primitive follows independently from v=t-s and agrees algebraically with the original unsplit quadratic.

obligations.target: PROOF_KO.md sections 3,5; endpoints and left limits
obligations.reason: F is continuous for bounded finite piecewise-polynomial forcing; only the initial hR0 term can jump downward. Stored base-cell polynomials have the actual left value and right left limit. Actual right endpoints use the new kernel coefficient. All-zero derivative gives a constant polynomial without a continuum root list; a nonzero constant derivative has no roots; a linear derivative has its exact rational root. The quadratic derivative is split at its rational strict-interior vertex, making each branch strictly monotone. Endpoint roots, vertex double roots and strict sign-changing branches are handled separately.

obligations.target: PROOF_KO.md section 5; root coverage and width
obligations.reason: A monotone branch with a zero endpoint has no further root in its interior. A branch with strictly opposite endpoint signs has exactly one root. At most two branches require bisection; each exact midpoint zero ends early, otherwise 96 halvings give width<=2^-96. Roots near endpoints or each other and double roots remain covered by exact sign and zero tests.

For rootbox width w, the chain factor in dP(a+w*y)/dy is w. Restricting the quadratic derivative gives 3|c[i+1]-c[i]|<=w*M_B and hence max(c)-min(c)<=w*M_B. The midpoint is inside that coefficient hull. Taking maxima of exact candidates and midpoint/hull pairs gives 0<=U-L<=M_B*2^-96<=3*Cmax*2^-96. The latter inequality uses B_i>=0.

Endpoints and all interior derivative roots cover the maximum of each continuous cubic extension. Downward actual right jumps cannot exceed its left limit. The maximum of local lower/upper pairs encloses the observation-cell supremum and its gap is at most the maximum local gap. Outward dyadic conversion adds at most 2*2^-128 to the total width.

Quadratic degree elevation produces the stated four nonnegative coefficients. Direct beta integrals give beta0=1/(n+4), beta1=3/((n+3)(n+4)), beta2=6/((n+2)(n+3)(n+4)), beta3=6/((n+1)(n+2)(n+3)(n+4)). At n=0 each equals1/4, so d=0 gives duration/4.

Changing u to 1-u gives W_i(z)=exp(z)W_(3-i)(-z). Positive integer floor/ceil recurrences bound each nonnegative exponential term at rounded argument bounds. The omitted term x_hi^97/97! and ratio x_hi/98<1 give the displayed geometric tail. beta_i<=1 permits the same conservative tail for all moments. Positive products, reciprocal positive exp and outward rounding preserve inclusion.

The comparison Y has derivative exp(d_c*u)(d_c E_left+Qmax), of constant sign even for negative d_c, so max(left,Y(right)) bounds its whole cell. The tighter polynomial endpoint is passed forward separately.

The original-source J primitives and four exact sample interpolation values construct the cubic independently of Simpson assembly. Monomial moments m!*duration^(m+1)*phi_(m+1) produce an independent endpoint recurrence, and analytic discriminant roots provide independent critical coverage. Decimal160 with the frozen1e-80 guard is numerical corroboration, not an interval proof.
